_doc: Where the native iPhone rewrite stands, stage by stage. Read live by JatBot OS > Status > Jacked (agent repo scripts/project-pages.json, sources iosLocal/iosRemote; parser frontend/src/jatbot/projectPages.ts iosRewrite()). Any job that moves a stage updates THIS file in the same commit: set status, edit summary/detail, add commits, bump updated (ISO time with offset; the page shows whichever of the working-tree and origin/main copies has the later updated). status: done | gate (blocked on Mr. Roni, his turn) | active (being built now) | todo. Order = build order (IOS_REWRITE_PLAN.md 'Build order'). Plain words only: this text is shown to Mr. Roni as is.

stages.title: Kickoff and first screen
stages.summary: Xcode project with the login and sign-up screen, written on the desktop.
detail: Login and sign-up in Jacked's dark and teal look, session kept in the Keychain, a placeholder signed-in screen that reads your own profile to prove the login works.
Talks to Supabase with plain web calls, no extra package.
The networking part compiles on the desktop and passes 16 of 16 live read-only checks (re-run 2026-11-04 evening).
The screens and the Xcode project file have only been read through, never built in Xcode.

stages.title: Decisions locked
stages.summary: iOS 17 and up, one App Store listing with the watch app, plain web calls.
detail: Oldest supported: iOS 17, iPhone XS and newer.
One App Store listing for the iPhone app and Phil's Apple Watch app. The bundle id and team in the project are still a placeholder.
Plain web calls to Supabase, not the supabase-swift package (your final answer, twice).
Account deletion waits until the basics below work.

stages.title: First build in Xcode
stages.summary: Builds in Xcode on the Mac and runs in the iPhone simulator.
detail: Built with a real xcodebuild on the Mac and run in the simulator on 2026-11-06; screenshot and video were sent to you.
Agent jobs now build and screenshot it on the Mac themselves, signed in as a throwaway test account, never yours.

stages.title: Your workout history on the Home screen
stages.summary: Read-only: workout history, streak and calendar on the iPhone Home screen, plus the tab bar.
detail: Signs in, downloads the saved data and keeps a copy on the phone, one copy per account, so it opens offline.
Home shows the streak box, the month calendar (tap a day to see what was trained), Start Workout and the last 6 workouts; tap one for every exercise and set.
Checked in the iPhone simulator next to the web app, both signed in to the same throwaway test account: same streak, same best, same trained days, same workouts.
Writes nothing yet. Start Workout says logging is the next step.
Not on Home yet: the monthly recap card (comes with Metrics), the Suggested today card (comes with routines), the Gym years view.

stages.title: Safe saving
stages.summary: The careful save layer is in: the iPhone can rename a past workout and the web app shows it.
detail: Every save reads the latest copy from the server first, merges it with what's on the phone using the same rules as the web app, and only writes if nobody else saved in between. If someone did, it reads again and merges again.
The merge rules are a direct copy of the web app's. Checked on the Mac: 2,014 sample cases run through both the web app's code and the iPhone's code gave the same result every time.
Checked for real in the iPhone simulator on the throwaway test account: renamed a workout, the web app shows the new name, nothing else in the account changed.
Also forced the worst case: another device saved a workout while the iPhone was mid-save. Both the other workout and the iPhone's rename survived.
If the phone is offline, the change stays on the phone and goes out on the next sync.
Not yet: updating the friends leaderboard numbers after a save. That needs the stats math, which comes with workout logging and Metrics.

stages.title: Workout logging
stages.summary: Logging works like the web app: the iPhone logged workouts on the throwaway test account and the web app shows the same sets, volume and PRs.
detail: Start an empty workout, one of your routines, or a past day from the calendar ("Log a workout for this day"). Starting a new one while another is open asks first, like the web app.
On each exercise: weight and reps, check sets off, the greyed numbers from last time, a PREV column, add and remove sets, the rest timer with -15/+15/skip, the plate calculator.
Same buttons as the web app: Single/Both for one-arm lifts, Bodyweight/+ Added/- Assist for pull-ups and dips, Sec/Min/Hr for holds, miles and stopwatch-style minutes with the pace for runs.
Switch an exercise, pair two as a superset, reorder them, and a note per exercise that's remembered next time (saved through the careful save layer, the web app showed it).
One gold star per exercise on the record set, plus PR, Go up and Lighter badges, exactly the web app's rules. The finish summary shows new and suggested PRs and the moved-up / consider-lighter notes.

Checked side by side in the iPhone simulator and the web app, same test account: the same stars, badges, totals and pace, and finished workouts show up in the web app with the same sets, volume and PRs.
The finish math is copied from the web app and checked on the Mac: 600 of 600 random workouts came out identical.
Not checked: the Apple Watch, since no watch is attached to the simulator. The watch reads the same saved data the web app does.
Moved to the next step, because they need the muscle-group and stats math that comes with Metrics: the Suggested today card on Home and updating your leaderboard numbers after a save.

stages.title: Library, stats and friends
stages.summary: In progress: Library and Routines are in and checked against the web app. Metrics and badges, then friends and the leaderboard, come next.
detail: Library done: search, the muscle chips, favourites first then what you've used, the PR on each row, and the exercise page with photos, your suggested PR, recent top weights and the how-to steps. Favourite, hide and create a custom exercise all save through the careful save layer.
Routines done: your routines in their sections like the web app, new, edit and delete a routine (it files itself into a section the same way), and Trusted Programs with + Add to Routines.

Checked on the throwaway test account, side by side with the web app: the same list order, PRs and chart numbers; a favourite, a custom exercise, a new routine and an added program made on the iPhone all showed up in the web app.

Not on the iPhone yet: editing an exercise, resetting a PR, a photo for a custom exercise, Today's pick on Trusted Programs, renaming and reordering sections. The exercise list needs one online open to download, then works offline.

Still to do in this step: Metrics and badges (the stats math gets checked number for number against the web app), friends and the leaderboard (tested between two throwaway accounts), and the Home extras that need that math: Suggested today, monthly recap, Gym years, the gold PR lines on the calendar day view, and updating the leaderboard numbers after each saved workout.

stages.title: Settings and account deletion
stages.summary: Profile and settings, and the delete-my-account button Apple requires.
detail: App Store blocker: Apple rejects apps that let you sign up but not delete the account.
Needs a small server change, which waits for your go before it runs live.
Waiting until the basics above work, your call.

stages.title: iPhone-only extras and the watch
stages.summary: Rest timer on the Lock Screen, Apple Health, Face ID, live workout with the Apple Watch.
detail: At least one real native feature helps with Apple's review and is the reason to have an app at all.
Apple Health is also the smart-scale path you asked about.

stages.title: App Store paperwork
stages.summary: Privacy policy, privacy labels, screenshots, age rating, trademark check on the name Jacked.
detail: The trademark check is better done early: renaming after launch is expensive.
Privacy labels must match what the app really collects: username, optional email, workouts, body weight, birthday, sex, photo.

stages.title: Submit to the App Store
detail: Needs everything above.
The signing team and final bundle id, the upload and the review are steps only you can do on the Mac and in App Store Connect.
